record.file_problem: The README and file list are available; the listed paper.pdf and result files were not read.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports applying the mean-difference refusal-direction ablation method to Gemma 2 2B IT and gives refusal-rate results, making this a direct test on a new model.
record.gate_note: The README reports harmful and harmless refusal rates for the final ablation and screened layers. Direction-norm values are not included as rows because the text presents them as a layer profile, not a behavioral outcome. The repository lists result JSON files, but their contents were not read.
record.test_reason: It applies the original difference-in-means extraction and all-layer directional ablation to Gemma 2 2B IT. It reports harmful and harmless refusal rates before and after ablation, the same kind of measure as the original. The model is new and the evaluation is weaker: AdvBench in-distribution, prefix matching only, no safety classifier.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors claim complete refusal elimination in Gemma 2 2B IT via a single mean-difference direction at layer 23, with harmless compliance preserved. They argue the linear refusal representation is a property of the Gemma training pipeline, not a Gemma 1 artifact. That second point is asserted, not tested.
record.recipe_differences: The README says it extends the original methodology. It uses Gemma 2 2B IT, AdvBench (128 prompts, described as in-distribution), 30 refusal prefixes, no safety classifier, and layer 23 at position -1; the comparison lists Gemma 1's held-out JailbreakBench evaluation, 12 prefixes, LlamaGuard2, and layer 10 at position -2. Repository type: replication/extension with a paper and reported results.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported layer changes the effect: six of ten screened layers achieve complete harmful-refusal removal, while layers 17, 21, 22 and 24 leave some harmful refusals.
record.problems: The README reports an AdvBench evaluation described as in-distribution, and does not report broad general-capability tests or uncertainty estimates. The paper and raw result files are listed but were not read for this repo record.
record.rows_left_out: Direction-norm profile values are omitted because they are not behavioral outcomes; the README's image-only layer summary is not separately recorded because the layer-effectiveness table gives the associated rates.

untested.parts: Adding the direction to induce refusal; general capability preservation (no benchmark or coherence check); held-out evaluation set; classifier-based judging.
No transfer of a direction across models or languages. The direction is re-extracted on Gemma 2.
All. The claim about the training pipeline is an interpretation, not a test.

missing.what: Contents of paper.pdf and replication_results.json. These may hold activation-addition (induction) results, capability checks, or completions used to verify the prefix-matching judge.
Size of the screening prompt subset and its harmless baseline. Rates suggest about 26 prompts.

record.verdict_notes: The layer-sweep rows were reclassified as selection values. With them, the record's limits_scope label for layers 17/21/22/24 was dropped: failing to remove refusal fully at non-selected candidate layers matches the original's selection procedure and does not qualify V1. Main caveats are in the setup, not the results. Evaluation is in-distribution (AdvBench was likely used for both extraction and evaluation), refusal is judged by prefix matching with no safety classifier, n=128, and there is no uncertainty or capability check. So 'complete ablation' may overstate the result. The layer-table harmless rate at L23 (0.0%) conflicts with the final evaluation (0.8%), likely because they used different subsets. Only the README was read.

versions.untested_parts: The README tests directional removal, not adding the direction; it reports harmless false-refusal rates but does not test general capabilities broadly.
No weight-edit or released-model abliteration result is reported.
No attack suppression or training against ablation is tested.
No comparison of single-direction, affine, cone, or multiple-direction accounts is reported.
No separate harmfulness-judgment measure is reported.
The README evaluates a direction extracted for Gemma 2; it does not test transfer of the same direction across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct models.
No comparison of refusal training methods or training stages is reported.
